title: The Discipline of Persuasion
text:
An argumentative essay is not merely a statement of opinion; it is a structured attempt to persuade a skeptical reader. Its force depends on the writer's capacity to anticipate objections and address them before they are raised. A weak essay, by contrast, tends to rely on emotional appeal while neglecting the evidence that would make a claim credible.

Consider, for instance, a writer who argues that cities should invest in public transport. A compelling version of this essay would acknowledge the cost of such investment and then demonstrate, with concrete data, that the long-term benefits outweigh the initial expense. Such a concession does not weaken the thesis; rather, it lends the writer authority.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what tends to characterize a weak essay?
options: Its failure to acknowledge any opinion
Reliance on emotional appeal while neglecting evidence
The absence of a clear conclusion

questions.text: In the example, what must the essay demonstrate with concrete data?
options: That the cost of investment is zero
That long-term benefits outweigh the initial expense
That the writer is an expert in engineering

questions.text: Why does the passage say that conceding a point lends the writer authority?
options: Concessions reveal that the writer has no real thesis
Acknowledging objections shows the writer has considered the issue fairly
Readers prefer essays that avoid all counterarguments
Concessions allow the writer to avoid providing evidence

questions.text: The passage implies that a skeptical reader is most likely to be persuaded when the writer:
options: relies on the strongest emotional language available
addresses objections the reader is already likely to hold
avoids discussing the costs of the proposed policy
presents a claim without any supporting data

vocabulary.definition: to foresee or expect something before it happens
reasons or arguments raised against a claim
able to be believed or trusted
an admission that a point made by others has some validity

paragraph_translations: Um ensaio argumentativo não é apenas uma declaração de opinião; é uma tentativa estruturada de persuadir um leitor cético. Sua força depende da capacidade do autor de antecipar objeções e abordá-las antes que surjam. Um ensaio fraco, em contraste, tende a depender de apelos emocionais enquanto negligencia as evidências que tornariam uma afirmação crível.

Considere, por exemplo, um autor que defende que as cidades devem investir em transporte público. Uma versão convincente desse ensaio reconheceria o custo de tal investimento e, em seguida, demonstraria, com dados concretos, que os benefícios de longo prazo superam a despesa inicial. Tal concessão não enfraquece a tese; ao contrário, confere autoridade ao autor.
